title: Compiler Infrastructure & Custom Bytecode Virtual Machines (PYTH_181_S1 to PYTH_181_S8)

slides.title: Building a Bytecode VM in Python
slides.prompt: Custom interpreters compile high-level ASTs into bytecode instruction sequences, executed sequentially by a virtual machine loop using an evaluation stack.

slides.title: Stack Machine Operations
slides.prompt: Fill in the stack operation name used to remove and return the top value from an evaluation stack.

slides.title: Stack-Based vs Register-Based VMs
slides.prompt: What is the key structural difference between a stack-based VM (like CPython) and a register-based VM (like Lua JIT)?
options: Stack VMs use an implicit push/pop memory stack, whereas register VMs use explicit indexed registers for instructions
Stack VMs compile code to binary files, while register VMs evaluate text source directly
Register VMs cannot execute branching or loop control flow statements
Stack VMs require GPU acceleration to process bytecode
slides.correctAnswer: Stack VMs use an implicit push/pop memory stack, whereas register VMs use explicit indexed registers for instructions

slides.title: Opcode Representation
slides.prompt: Fill in the standard library module used to define enumerated constants for VM opcodes.

slides.title: CPython Instruction Pointer
slides.prompt: What role does the Instruction Pointer (or Program Counter) play inside an execution engine loop?
options: It tracks the offset address of the next bytecode instruction to be fetched and executed
It counts the remaining memory allocated to thread stacks
It measures function execution duration in milliseconds
slides.correctAnswer: It tracks the offset address of the next bytecode instruction to be fetched and executed

slides.title: Lexical Tokenizing with SRE
slides.prompt: Fill in the standard Python module function used to match lexical patterns when building custom compiler tokenizers.

slides.title: Bytecode Jump Targets
slides.prompt: How are conditional control flow statements (`if`/`else`) represented inside bytecode instructions?
options: As conditional jump opcodes that update the instruction pointer to a specific target offset
By creating duplicate copies of the virtual machine process
By writing temporary Python files to disk
As asynchronous futures resolved by an event loop
slides.correctAnswer: As conditional jump opcodes that update the instruction pointer to a specific target offset
